articles.title: AI Agents Are Using Credit Cards. Where Does That Leave Crypto?
articles.text:
AI agents are using credit cards. Where does that leave crypto?
AI agents are already using credit cards to transact, raising questions about where crypto fits in the emerging agent economy.
The idea that crypto will become the default payment choice for autonomous AI agents is widespread in the industry. The thesis is that because AI agents can’t open bank accounts and need to make lots of transactions, they will inexorably gravitate to instant, decentralized and low cost crypto payments.
But the credit card industry has no intention of letting that happen.
The Wall Street Journal reported on Nov. 19 that AI agents are already using credit cards to make purchases on consumers’ behalf, and banks and payment companies are racing to accommodate them. Crypto trader and co-host of the 1000x podcast Jonah Van Bourg posted a screenshot, and commented:
“Agents will not use crypto rails. The book is closed on blockchain as a solution, outside of niche back office applications. Its only use cases are sov, privacy, and ledger stuff. Sad.”
But experts argue the jury is still out. Professor emeritus of finance at Marquette University, David Krause, tells Magazine that credit cards offer some advantages, but high costs could be their downfall in certain scenarios.
“Credit cards were built for a world where a human decides to pay, so when an agent pays $0.005 for an API call, the fixed fees on card rails are 50x the transaction itself.”
Stablecoins, he says, make much more sense for “those situations involving micropayments.”
The payment rail depends on what the agent is buying
Credit card payments are the default for most human-initiated transactions on the web. So an agent tasked with booking a flight or a hotel room may also default to this type of payment as well.
Related: DeepSeek developing AI agent requiring less human input: Report
“When an agent books your flight or reorders your groceries, it’s acting for a person, at a merchant that already accepts cards, with consumer protections people expect, like chargebacks,” Lewis Nurcombe, chief revenue officer at WalletConnect, tells Magazine.
Visa’s recent paper on the rise of agentic commerce says tokenization can give agents permission to transact without needing to expose the cardholder’s underlying payment details, and spending controls can restrict the purchases they can make.
So when the merchant already accepts cards and has familiar mechanisms for handling disputed transactions, it’s hard to argue the virtues of introducing an entirely new payment system.
But the economics start to change when agents begin paying other machines.
Stablecoins make sense when machines pay machines
AI agents may create a new economy of machine-to-machine transactions, where agents buy access to a dataset, request computing power, or pay to access a single piece of information. Many of these transactions may only be worth a fraction of a cent and potentially need to occur thousands of times without a human approving each one.
“If an agent wants to pay a few cents for one API call or one piece of data, card fees don’t make sense,” Aitor Argomaniz, chief executive of AI payments company Nevermined, tells Magazine.
That’s because card networks were designed around transactions big enough to absorb fixed processing fees, rather than micro-payments.
Stablecoins offer a different model. Agents can hold funds in a wallet, make payments programmatically and settle transactions onchain without going through a conventional checkout process.
Nurcombe says that stablecoins are most useful “wherever the transaction is too small, too frequent or too global for cards to make sense.”
Protocols like x402 let services request payment as part of an internet interaction. That allows an agent to pay for access to a resource rather than subscribe to a service or manually complete a checkout.
x402 is an open, neutral standard for internet-native payments. Source: x402
Nevermined compared 100 API calls priced at 10 cents each. Using a conventional card via Stripe would not be an option as the payments infrastructure network rejects charges under $0.50. But using stablecoins, the company estimates the same 100 payments would cost around 10 cents in total using Coinbase’s x402 facilitator on Base.
That doesn’t mean crypto payments will automatically win however, as a number of microtransactions could be aggregated into a single card payment. Stablecoin transactions also carry costs related to infrastructure, conversion, custody and liquidity.
The Bank for International Settlements (BIS) found that stablecoin transfers can still incur trading, conversion and withdrawal fees, while limited liquidity between stablecoins and local currencies can add further friction.
Who takes responsibility when an AI agent makes a mistake?
In the transition to agentic finance, there’s a more fundamental question to overcome: who is responsible when an agent gets something wrong?
Related: Banks are banning AI agents over security... and competition concerns
“I tell my students the real question isn’t ‘crypto or cards,’ it’s who solves the agent identity and liability attribution issues,” Krause says.
“That’s because the first time an agent books the wrong flight, someone has to own that dispute, and that’s a 50-year competency the crypto world hasn’t built yet.”
One partial solution is a separate wallet funded with a limited amount of money that could prevent an agent from accidentally draining a user’s main account.
WalletConnect is developing ways for users to give agents access to dedicated wallets while retaining control over the rest of their funds.
“The most an agent can ever spend is what the person chose to give it,” Nurcombe says.
But spending limits only mitigate the damage. They can’t determine who is liable when an agent makes an unauthorized purchase, buys the wrong service or falls victim to manipulation. Nor do they provide the kind of resolution consumers expect from established payment providers.
Nevermined compared 100 API calls priced at 10 cents each. Source: Nevermined.
That may mean banks and card networks have an advantage beyond just having more merchants on their systems; they already have relationships with customers, businesses and regulators, as well as established processes for handling disputes.
Krause says that stacks the odds in traditional finance’s favor. “My bet is the large TradFi players will ultimately win,” he says. “They’re the ones with funding access and are positioned to straddle the divide and offer a hybrid version.”
Nevermined supports payments using both cards and stablecoins, and Argomaniz expects the two systems to coexist, “at least for the next few years.”
Crypto could power the plumbing without owning the market
This is where Van Bourg’s argument becomes harder for the crypto industry to dismiss — even if stablecoins are useful for machine-to-machine payments, established payment networks could just incorporate them without handing over control of the customer relationship.
So an agent might interact with Visa or Mastercard while the networks use blockchain infrastructure behind the scenes.
That would effectively turn blockchain into payment plumbing without businesses or consumers needing to hold crypto or interact with a decentralized protocol.
Mastercard completed its acquisition of stablecoin infrastructure provider BVNK in August, in a deal announced at up to $1.8 billion, giving Mastercard the infrastructure to connect fiat and onchain payments.
So, while AI agents could use blockchain-based payments where existing rails struggle, crypto could find itself powering the agent economy without capturing much of its value.

articles.title: BTCS sold more Ethereum than it has left to repay $43.8 million in debt
articles.text:
Quick Take
- BTCS said it sold about 27,300 ETH on Nov. 20, using the proceeds to repay $43.8 million on Aave.
- In preliminary figures, BTCS put its remaining holdings at about 24,245 ETH and its Aave debt at about $10.5 million.
- Imperium, which supplied about 86% of third-quarter revenue, earns no liquidity pool fees on its withdrawn capital.
BTCS sold about 27,300 Ethereum (ETH) on Nov. 20 and used the proceeds to repay $43.8 million of debt on Aave, a decentralized lending protocol, the company disclosed on Nov. 23.
The amount sold exceeded the roughly 24,245 ETH it said it held afterward, based on a preliminary, unaudited estimate.
The sell-off also prompted BTCS’s decentralized finance business, Imperium, to pull its capital out of liquidity pools. That put fees on the withdrawn capital on hold at a business that accounted for most of the company’s third-quarter revenue.
The two decisions were linked by how BTCS financed Imperium. A day before the sale, the company reported about $54 million in Aave debt, and it borrowed stablecoins against some of its Ethereum and used the proceeds primarily to fund Imperium’s liquidity pool positions.
BTCS said it monitors the position and can adjust its borrowing as the value of its ETH collateral changes. A drop in the value of pledged ETH can put that collateral at risk of liquidation.
BTCS Chief Executive Charles Allen said management chose to sell Ethereum and repay Aave to reduce that risk and preserve the company’s ability to meet its obligations on senior secured convertible notes.
He said:
“Selling at these prices came at a real cost to the Company and its shareholders.”
BTCS reported that about $10.5 million remained on Aave after the repayment, at a loan-to-value ratio of roughly 32%, which measures the outstanding loan against the value of its collateral.
In the same preliminary, unaudited update, BTCS reported aggregate principal on its convertible notes of about $17.9 million, with maturities in May and July 2027.
Imperium’s Ethereum pool fee pause
BTCS’s Nov. 12 earnings release showed that the division generated $3.5 million in third-quarter revenue, about 86% of BTCS’s $4.1 million total.
The company reported $40.9 million in liquidity pool positions at the end of September, up from $7.6 million at the end of June as Imperium expanded its strategy across Ethereum and Base.
The company says Imperium earns no pool fees on that capital while it sits outside the pools. Management still plans to focus the business on Imperium and intends to put the capital back to work when it judges conditions have improved. It gave no date for doing so.

articles.title: Aave’s USDC loans surge 36% to $2.6 billion as liquid collateral share plunges
articles.text:
Quick Take
- TokenLogic proposes raising Aave’s USDC backstop target to 45.8 million USDC while cutting the extra reward APY at target to 2.5%.
- At historical exit rates, Nov. 17 cooldowns would leave USDC about 240,000 above its proposed target and USDT at 91% of its target.
- CryptoKeyhole’s Nov. 23 contract reading valued USDC stake at $51.3 million and USDT stake at $46.8 million, with cooldowns unreported.
Aave DAO service provider TokenLogic has proposed on Nov. 20 raising the USDC stake target for Umbrella, the protocol’s bad-debt backstop on Ethereum, from 38.84 million to 45.8 million USDC.
The proposal would also cut the extra reward APY at that target from 3.14% to 2.5%.
If holders withdrew from the Nov. 17 cooldown queue at the historical rate with no other changes to stake, about 46 million USDC would remain staked, roughly 240,000 USDC above the proposed target. Under the same test, USDT would fall short.
The proposal would extend Umbrella rewards for USDC, USDT and WETH past their Dec. 2 expiry through April 2, 2027. TokenLogic plans to gather forum feedback before advancing the renewal to a formal Aave Improvement Proposal.
Aave’s ten latest governance proposals showed no corresponding vote or execution as of Nov. 23.
Umbrella stakers put their interest-bearing Aave deposits at risk to cover bad debt. To leave, they first start a 20-day cooldown, then have two days to withdraw.
Across cooldown windows closed through Oct. 26, TokenLogic found that holders withdrew 44% of the USDC and 55% of the USDT they had queued.
On Nov. 17, Holders had staked 53.75 million USDC, with 32.6% in cooldown. At that balance, withdrawals of about 45% from the queue would bring USDC stake down to the proposed target, only slightly above the 44% historically withdrawn.
The USDT vault held nearly 59 million staked, with 55.4% queued. Applying its historical exit share leaves about 41 million USDT, or 91% of its proposed 45.2 million target.
At historical withdrawal rates, the Nov. 17 model leaves USDC 240,000 above target and USDT nearly 4.2 million below.
On Nov. 23, CryptoKeyhole valued the USDC and USDT stakes at about $51.3 million and $46.8 million, respectively, using readings from the Ethereum contracts. Its dashboard reported stake totals without cooldown balances, so withdrawal estimates are tied to Nov. 17.
A bigger loan book changes the target
Active USDC loans on Aave V3 Ethereum Core rose about 36%, from $1.9 billion on June 3 to $2.6 billion on Nov. 17, according to TokenLogic. USDe and sUSDe together rose from 4% to 12% of the collateral backing those loans.
Meanwhile, the share of collateral in the group of highly liquid assets TokenLogic tracks fell from 88.5% to 77.6%.
Against that November loan book, the existing target amounts to 1.5% of USDC borrowing. The proposal would lift that share to 1.77%, below the roughly 2% used in June. TokenLogic also proposed cutting USDT’s extra APY at target from 3.17% to 2.5%.
The 2.50% applies to the additional Umbrella reward at the target stake level. At the higher stake recorded on Nov. 17, the proposed rules would pay about 1.76% in annualized extra rewards.
TokenLogic put the total annualized yield, including deposit interest, at 7% on average over the seven days through Nov. 17.
The Aave DAO takes the first loss up to 1.3 million USDC. Beyond that offset, Umbrella can slash the USDC stake designated for the same Ethereum Core reserve and send the slashed assets to the Aave Collector to cover the deficit.
The loss-absorbing buffer comes from what holders stake, and ordinary Aave suppliers draw withdrawals from the lending reserve’s available USDC.
If the renewal takes effect, lending yields and the share of queued stake that leaves will help determine whether Umbrella can sustain the bigger buffer at the lower reward setting.

articles.title: Tom Lee Says Ethereum Is as Scarce as Bitcoin—And Bitmine Just Bought More
articles.text:
In brief
- Bitmine bought another 7,819 ETH, raising holdings to 6,085,564 ETH, or 4.98% of supply—99% of the way to its “Alchemy of 5%” goal.
- Chairman Tom Lee pitched ETH as “hard money,” noting its 0.90% annualized supply growth roughly matches Bitcoin’s 0.82% and undercuts Solana (7.6%).
- Total holdings stood at $11.1 billion, and the latest buy landed amid a crypto market rebound.
Bitmine Immersion Technologies kept its weekly Ethereum buying streak alive, adding 7,819 ETH worth roughly $13.8 million, as chairman Tom Lee leaned on a new argument for the battered token: its supply grows no faster than Bitcoin’s, making it just as much “hard money.”
The NYSE-listed company said Monday its holdings reached 6,085,564 ETH, worth roughly $10.4 billion at a reference price of $1,713 per coin, as of Nov. 22.
That’s 4.98% of Ethereum’s 122.2 million token supply, leaving Bitmine 99% of the way to its goal of owning 5% of the network, the “Alchemy of 5%” target it has chased for 17 months. The firm has bought Ethereum every week since launching its treasury strategy on June 30, 2025.
Did you know?
You can now act on the news you read: Go long or short Ethereum with perpetual futures, all from your Decrypt Money Account.
Lee’s pitch this week centered on scarcity. Since Bitmine pivoted to Ethereum in mid-2025, he said, ETH’s supply has grown just 0.90% on an annualized basis, roughly in line with Bitcoin’s 0.82%, meaning “both are ‘hard money’ measured in supply growth.” (Disclosure: Tom Lee is one of several investors in Dastan, Decrypt’s parent company.)
He contrasted that with more inflationary rivals, citing annualized supply growth of 7.6% for Solana, 5.4% for XRP, and 2.9% for Cardano. The framing builds on Ethereum co-founder Vitalik Buterin’s recent declaration that ETH is a store of value, which Lee has repeatedly invoked.
Counting cash, other tokens and “moonshot” investments, Bitmine’s total holdings stood at $11.1 billion, including 216 Bitcoin, $384 million in cash and marketable securities, a $180 million stake in Beast Industries and a $54 million position in Eightco Holdings.
ETH price on November 29, 4:59PM UTC
Bitmine remains the world’s largest Ethereum treasury and the second-largest crypto treasury overall, behind Michael Saylor’s Strategy, which the release said holds 849,327 BTC.
Strategy also kept buying through the downturn, recently adding $30 million in Bitcoin while shifting $1 billion from its dollar reserve to a cash pot.
The purchase lands as crypto claws back some ground after a bruising November. Bitcoin traded around $62,700 on Monday, up about 3.2% on the day, with Ethereum near $1,769, up 3.5%, as risk appetite steadied.
The rebound coincided with a dramatic reversal at Nvidia, which reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO just days after its board had ruled out his return, lifting sentiment across the AI-linked assets that crypto increasingly tracks.
Bitmine has 5,227,037 ETH, about 86% of its holdings, staked through its MAVAN platform, with projected annualized staking revenue of roughly $245 million.

articles.title: Critics of Netflix’s FTX Drama Cite Obama’s Producer Credit
articles.text:
Critics of Netflix’s FTX drama point to Obama’s producer credit
Series creator Graham Moore said he invented a scene in which Changpeng Zhao urges Alameda Research to trade ahead of FTX customers’ orders.
Critics who say Netflix’s new FTX drama favors Sam Bankman-Fried over Binance co-founder Changpeng “CZ” Zhao have pointed to former US President Barack Obama’s role as an executive producer.
DRW founder Don Wilson said Sunday that Netflix’s FTX drama The Altruists portrayed Bankman-Fried too sympathetically at the expense of Zhao.
In the fourth episode, Zhao’s character urges Bankman-Fried and Caroline Ellison to give Alameda Research advance access to FTX customers’ orders so it can trade ahead of them.
Series creator Graham Moore identified the scene as fiction in a Friday essay for Vulture. Moore wrote that he believed the pressure the pair faced was real, though “there’s no evidence that CZ ever specifically pressured FTX to front-run.”
Zhao called a clip from the series “complete BS” on Friday, a day after the eight-episode drama premiered. Investment research firm Farside Investors also singled out the front-running scene, saying the show cast Zhao as the villain.
Critics point to the Obamas’ producer credits
Wilson called the clip an “epic fail by Netflix.” In a second post, he cited the former US president’s executive producer credit. Netflix lists both Barack and Michelle Obama as executive producers and names Moore and Jacqueline Hoyt as showrunners.
In a Sunday post on X, an account called StarPlatinum pointed to the Obamas’ producer credits and Bankman-Fried’s donations to Democrats. The post did not offer evidence that the donations influenced the show.
Related: Sam Bankman-Fried wrote to actor portraying him in Netflix series
Bankman-Fried made about $40 million in publicly reported political donations during the 2022 election cycle, mostly to Democratic candidates and groups. Federal prosecutors later said he also used FTX customer funds to make political contributions to candidates from both parties.
What Ellison told the jury about FTX’s collapse
In November 2022, Zhao announced that Binance would sell its holdings of FTT, FTX’s token.
At Bankman-Fried’s 2023 trial, Ellison, Alameda’s former CEO, said she thought Zhao’s announcement “contributed to the situation.” She said FTX collapsed primarily because Alameda could not repay more than $10 billion in FTX customer funds.
Bankman-Fried was sentenced to 25 years in prison in 2024 for orchestrating a fraud that took more than $8 billion from FTX customers.
FTX’s bankruptcy estate sued Binance and Zhao in November 2024, seeking $1.76 billion paid in a 2021 share repurchase. The estate also sought damages over Zhao’s public statements. Binance called the claims “meritless.”
In July, US Bankruptcy Judge Karen Owens dismissed the claims over Zhao’s statements because FTX’s own misconduct barred them. She allowed the estate to pursue its separate claim over the buyback.

articles.title: XRP borrowers face a $207,500 tipping point as one vault dominates an $8 million market
articles.text:
Quick Take
- Morpho showed one Sentora vault supplied 99.99% of the RLUSD in its Ethereum FXRP market on Nov. 23.
- About 207,500 RLUSD of additional borrowing would take utilization to 90% at unchanged supply, with 1 million RLUSD available.
- One wallet posted 3,000 FXRP to borrow 1,500 RLUSD, while Sentora moved funds out of the market in separate transactions.
A single Sentora vault supplied virtually all the Ripple USD (RLUSD) in Morpho’s Ethereum market for loans against wrapped XRP on Nov. 23.
The market showed about 7.1 million RLUSD in outstanding loans and 1 million RLUSD available for new loans. Borrowers use FXRP, a token backed by XRP, to borrow the RLUSD stablecoin.
Sentora’s lending decisions can change both how much credit is available and the interest rate on existing loans.
At about 13:08 UTC, Morpho’s market dashboard put the Sentora RLUSD Main vault’s contribution at about 8.15 million RLUSD, or 99.99% of the market’s supply as displayed.
Borrowers had used 87.45% of the funds supplied to the market, a measure Morpho calls utilization, and the dashboard showed a variable borrow rate of 4.99%.
Earlier on Nov. 23, one wallet posted 3,000 FXRP as collateral and borrowed 1,500 RLUSD in the same transaction, according to Morpho’s indexed activity.
Flare’s FXRP documentation describes FXRP as a tokenized representation of native XRP, and its FAssets system verifies XRP Ledger transactions used to mint FXRP and supports redemption for native XRP.
Flare’s August announcement describes how holders can mint FXRP on Flare, bridge it to Ethereum through the FAssets Portal or Stargate, and post it as collateral in this market. Anyone already holding the market’s FXRP on Ethereum can start at the collateral step.
A borrower’s position can be liquidated if its debt exceeds 77% of the collateral’s value, as measured by the market’s price feed. A drop in collateral value can push a borrower closer to that threshold even without taking out another loan.
In a separate Nov. 23 transaction, the market log shows the Sentora vault withdrew 7,147.88 RLUSD. The vault’s allocation history shows the same transaction moving funds in two other lending markets, one backed by USDe and the other by syrupUSDC.
A later withdrawal of 10,498.74 RLUSD from the FXRP market appears in both logs.
How Sentora can change XRP borrowing costs
The FXRP market made up just 2.41% of the funds allocated by the Sentora vault, which reported 338.36 million RLUSD in deposits and 95.27 million RLUSD in liquidity across the vault.
In October, the same market had about 8.53 million RLUSD from Sentora and a 10 million RLUSD allocation cap. By Nov. 23, the cap was 15 million RLUSD, while Sentora supplied about 8.15 million.
The available funds for new borrowers were the 1 million RLUSD already in the market. Morpho’s liquidity API showed zero additional RLUSD available at about 13:10 UTC through its Public Allocator, which can move funds from participating vaults when their settings permit it.
Other borrows or allocations can change the amount available before a transaction executes. That same reading showed that about 207,500 RLUSD of additional borrowing would bring the market to 90% utilization with supply unchanged.
The 90% mark is the reference point for Morpho’s interest-rate model. Borrowing can continue above that level while funds are available, with a steeper rate curve above the target.
If Sentora takes unborrowed RLUSD out of the market while debt stays constant, utilization rises, and the variable rate can climb without anyone taking out a fresh loan. Adding supply with debt unchanged gives new borrowers more room and can ease rates for existing borrowers.

And the FOMO contagion spread quickly to other tech stocks. Rival AMD jumped 8.91% to $462.09, while the iShares Semiconductor ETF (SOXX) surged 15% to $141.77.

Bitcoin joined the party, trading near $63,500 after dipping below $60,000 during Friday’s selloff. Ethereum climbed to about $1,790, and cash CFDs tracking the Nasdaq 100 and S&P 500 rebounded to roughly 26,950 and 7,285, respectively.
The catalyst was Nvidia’s announcement that its founder Jensen Huang had been reinstated as president, CEO and director, effective immediately. The board voted unanimously just six days after publicly ruling out his return—and even doubling down on their decision several times.
From ousted to back in charge
Huang resigned November 12 amid reports of extramarital relationships, including one with a businesswoman U.S. officials suspected of ties to Chinese intelligence. Beijing has denied the espionage allegation, and no public evidence has established that Huang knowingly passed company secrets to China.
Colette Kress, Nvidia’s finance chief, took over as interim CEO while the company launched a search for a permanent replacement. On November 17, board chair Harvey Jones said directors did not intend to reinstate Huang, despite a campaign for his return backed by Silicon Valley executives and President Donald Trump.
Monday’s reversal followed meetings with Huang and input from senior U.S. government officials. The board said it was satisfied with his candor and leadership ability and was confident his return posed “no national security risk,” though its independent investigation will continue.
“I can’t wait to get back to work,” Huang said in the statement. Kress will remain chief financial officer, and Jones will stay on as board chair.
“It tells us to some extent that Jensen Huang was too big to be fired,” Interactive Brokers strategist Steve Sosnick told Reuters.
Prediction markets were caught off guard, too. A Polymarket contract on Huang rejoining Nvidia by November 30 traded near 99% after the announcement, compared with roughly 3% shortly beforehand.
His return also tanked the probabilities of the AI bubble bursting. After his outsting, Polymarket odds skyrocketed to more than 70%, minutes after his reinstatement, the odds dropped to 14%.
Crypto rebounds, but Bitcoin still has work to do
The rally followed an ugly stretch for AI stocks. Nvidia closed Friday at $125.53, about 47.5% below its October high, while the Nasdaq lost roughly 10% over the previous week. Bitcoin fell toward $55,100 Friday night before staging a weekend recovery.
Monday’s bounce pushed Nvidia above the $166.19 closing price recorded on the day Huang resigned. Bitcoin, meanwhile, recovered the $63,000 area, but its daily chart still shows a bearish moving-average configuration and a relative strength index near 34, indicating that the recent relief rally has not erased the broader downtrend.
Overall, crypto traders are still timid but evidently don’t think this is the end of the world.
On the chart, Bitcoin faces initial resistance around $65,030, followed by $68,090. On the downside, $61,240 and the psychological $60,000 mark are immediate levels to watch; another break lower would put the recent $55,100 area back in focus.
Anthropic misses the rally
One of the few notable losers was Anthropic, whose stock slipped 3.16% to $85.81. That left the Claude developer about 25% below its post-IPO peak near $115, although still slightly above the $83 offering price set for its $81.34 billion public offering last Thursday. Nvidia itself committed about $10 billion to a separate, conditional private investment in Anthropic alongside the IPO.
The decline looks more like investors continuing to digest a pricey, volatile listing than a reaction to Huang’s reinstatement. But the internet has another theory: memes and posts have cast Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei as playing a role in Huang’s ouster because of his support towards open-weight models and his decision to buy Hugging Face, the world’s largest repository of open source AI models, to protect the ecosystem.
— Zephyr (@zephyr_z9) November 23, 2026
Huang championed broad access to open models, while Amodei has argued for tighter safeguards around powerful AI systems, especially warning against open source AI competing against close models like the ones his company develops, a position that has been widely criticized by influential figures in the AI scene like Yan Lecun who called his mindset “a new form of medieval obscurantism.”
Dario's spiel since GPT-2 has always been about hyping the dangers so that open models would be made illegal and *he* would stay in control.
He left OpenAI because he wasn't going to have control.
It's like the Ottoman Empire banning the printing press for Arabic so they would…
— Yann LeCun (@ylecun) November 22, 2026
Nvidia’s independent inquiry into the reported foreign intelligence effort remains open. Huang has also been asked to meet House investigators on December 1 and testify before a Senate panel on December 3.

articles.title: ECB to Let Banks Pledge More Tokenized Securities as Collateral
articles.text:
ECB to let banks pledge more tokenized securities as collateral
The ECB aims to start accepting securities issued on platforms licensed under the EU’s distributed ledger pilot program in June 2027.
The European Central Bank (ECB) approved a plan Monday to let banks borrow from euro area central banks against tokenized securities issued on platforms licensed under an EU pilot program.
The ECB plans to put the change into effect in June 2027, according to its announcement. The EU’s DLT Pilot Regime allows licensed platforms to handle trading or settlement of securities using distributed ledger technology.
Since March 30, banks have been able to pledge qualifying tokenized securities issued through central securities depositories that use distributed ledgers. Under Monday’s decision, a bank holding a qualifying bond issued on a licensed pilot platform could also use it to secure a central bank loan.
The securities must still meet the existing collateral rules of the Eurosystem, which comprises the ECB and the national central banks of the euro area. They must also be available to the Eurosystem through an approved link to a central securities depository that offers settlement on TARGET2-Securities, the Eurosystem’s securities settlement platform.
The Eurosystem expects to publish additional legal and operational requirements for the pilot platforms in spring 2027.
“A future-proof collateral framework must embrace new technologies without compromising on safety or the rigour of our risk assessment,” said ECB executive board member Isabel Schnabel.
The ECB said it is also exploring how banks could pledge securities issued and settled entirely on distributed ledgers. Through its Appia project, the Eurosystem plans to publish a blueprint in 2028 for how Europe’s tokenized wholesale financial markets could operate.
Related: EU taps industry to set standards for tokenized securities

The board voted unanimously to reinstate Huang as president, CEO and a board member, effective immediately, the company said on Monday. It followed "a series of discussions and meetings" with Huang, after which the board was satisfied with his "candor and ability to lead" the firm.

In reaching its decision, the board said it received input from "senior levels of the United States government," and based on that input, it is confident that Huang's reinstatement "poses no national security risk." The statement did not name the officials involved.

NVIDIA Board reinstates Jensen Huang as President, CEO and Board Director.

"I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment," Huang said in the statement. "I can't wait to get back to work."
A sharp reversal
The decision overturns the board's position from last week. "The Nvidia board does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO," Jones said on the company's November 17 earnings call, as Nvidia hired executive search firm Heidrick & Struggles to find a permanent replacement.
Hours earlier, Huang had offered to return if the board decided it was in the best interest of shareholders, employees, the company "and America." His comeback had drawn support from President Donald Trump and Elon Musk, even as CNBC reported that directors were not considering it.

Investigations continue
The independent directors' committee investigating whether Huang was the target of a foreign intelligence effort "will proceed to conclusion," Nvidia said, and Huang has said he will cooperate with it.
The company also pointed to its new National Security and Export Control Committee, made up of independent directors, and said it is searching for a chief compliance officer to oversee compliance across the company. Nvidia said it will keep cooperating with government investigations and inquiries.
Huang still faces scrutiny in Washington. House committees have asked him to sit for a closed-door interview on December 1, and Senate Banking Committee Chairman Tim Scott (R-SC) has asked him to testify at a public hearing on December 3.

- Economists expect the Fed’s preferred inflation gauge to show that prices rose 0.3% in October, down from 0.5% in September.
- Bitcoin hit $55,081 on Saturday, its lowest price since September 2024, and closed lower for a seventh straight week.
Tech futures hint at U-turn after week of selling
Nasdaq-100 futures rose 3.1% and S&P 500 futures gained 2.4% ahead of Monday’s US open after Friday’s tech sell-off.

articles.title: Inkling 2 Mini got 20 questions right but failed 4 out of 5 tests that required deeper thinking
articles.text:
Quick Take
- Plotly’s hosted test gave Inkling 2 Mini a perfect score on 20 routine questions and 36 of 43 overall.
- On one hidden-pattern question, the model ran 585 queries over about 48 minutes and still missed the answer.
- A local tester completed prompts of about 43,000 and 57,000 tokens on one 32 GB M5 MacBook Pro.
In a hosted test published by Plotly on Nov. 21, the AI model Inkling 2 Mini got all 20 routine data questions right.
On one question about a hidden pattern, it made 585 queries over about 48 minutes and repeated the same few queries dozens of times, but it still missed the pattern.
In Plotly’s benchmark, Inkling 2 Mini scored 36 of 43 overall and found one of five hidden patterns. Plotly found that on the hidden-pattern questions, the model often added up the biggest totals and stopped.
Plotly ran the model through its own analytics software, Plotly Studio Embedded, using a version hosted by Prime Intellect and accessed through OpenRouter. It reported one scored sample per model, combining results with reruns of 16 Inkling 2 Mini questions that encountered a provider outage.
What fits on a 32 GB MacBook
Thinking Machines Lab released the downloadable weights on Nov. 20 under the Apache 2.0 license. Its model card lists support for Apple silicon Macs with at least 32 GB of memory.
The card lists a context window of up to 1 million tokens, which measures how much information the model can handle at once. How much of that window is usable on a particular Mac depends on the memory needed to process the request.
In the Nov. 22 release notes for oMLX 0.8.3, the Mac software’s maintainers reported about 20% faster prompt processing and 10% to 13% faster generation than in 0.8.2 for a reduced-precision build on an M5 Max.
The update also lets oMLX refuse prompts on a 32 GB Mac when it estimates they would exceed the memory budget.
In a Nov. 23 follow-up, an oMLX issue reporter said prompts of about 43,000 and 57,000 tokens were completed on one 32 GB M5 MacBook Pro using the updated software and a reduced-precision build. Reported memory use peaked at 23 GB and 24 GB, respectively.
Once a request fits, a separate limit can stop an agent from spending more turns on the same few queries.
Thinking Machines Lab says it saw the model repeatedly check its work without making progress in internal tests. The lab recommends caps on generated tokens and on the number of turns an agent can take.

articles.title: MoldyRoost Ads Target Crypto Wallet Seed Phrases on iPhones
articles.text:
‘MoldyRoost’ ads can steal crypto wallet recovery phrases from iPhones
The campaign used at least 480 ad domains to target users in more than 47 countries and could infect a vulnerable iPhone with a single tap.
Hackers are using fake ads to spread malware that can steal crypto wallet recovery phrases from vulnerable iPhones, cybersecurity company Confiant said Friday.
Confiant, which calls the campaign MoldyRoost, linked at least 480 ad domains to it between May 12 and Nov. 17. The ads targeted users in more than 47 countries.
“Just loading the landing page of a MoldyRoost ad on a vulnerable iPhone is enough to get infected,” Confiant said in its report.
Google Threat Intelligence reported in March that hackers were using a tool called Coruna to target visitors to fake crypto sites. MoldyRoost bought ads to spread the same tool on sites unrelated to crypto, where tapping an ad could expose a recovery phrase saved on a vulnerable iPhone.
Coruna can search Apple Notes for wallet seed phrases and read QR codes in saved images. A thief who gets a seed phrase can use those words to open the wallet on another device and move the funds.
The campaign also used DarkSword, another tool that can steal wallet data, which Google researchers also warned of in March.
In a Nov. 6 warning about DarkSword, blockchain security firm CertiK urged iPhone users to update their software and keep seed phrases out of Notes, photos and screenshots. It also advised avoiding unfamiliar links and using a hardware wallet for larger holdings.
Related: SEC charges 8 firms over fake crypto platforms tied to $37M fraud

articles.title: Bitcoin’s supply squeeze narrative faces scrutiny after 11,000 BTC moves to Kraken
articles.text:
Quick Take
- More than 11,000 BTC moved from Coinbase and Binance into Kraken during Bitcoin's selloff, complicating expectations of a tightening supply.
- Kraken absorbed $478 million in net inflows, offsetting 41% of the $1.16 billion withdrawn from three major exchanges.
- With spot Bitcoin ETFs losing $669 million, Bitcoin's recovery faces a fresh test from US inflation data and weakening institutional demand.
More than 11,000 BTC moved from Coinbase and Binance to Kraken during Saturday's selloff, complicating Bitcoin's supply-squeeze narrative.
The five transactions, identified by Ask The Tape (ATT), came as major exchanges recorded hundreds of millions of dollars in net Bitcoin withdrawals, fueling expectations that fewer coins were available for trading.
However, the transfers revealed substantial movements between trading venues, with Bitcoin leaving some exchanges only to replenish reserves elsewhere.
Coinbase accounted for approximately 4,028 BTC across two transactions. The first delivered 2,177.79 BTC to Kraken-tagged addresses at 03:47 UTC, followed by another 1,850 BTC at 10:04 UTC.
Binance then transferred 7,000 BTC through three transactions: two transfers of 2,000 BTC each and a third involving 3,000 BTC.
The movements coincided with substantial differences in exchange flows reported by CryptoQuant.
Binance recorded $680 million in net Bitcoin withdrawals on Nov. 21, while Coinbase and Bybit registered $373 million and $103 million, respectively. Together, the three exchanges lost approximately $1.16 billion.
Kraken moved in the opposite direction, receiving $478 million in net inflows and offsetting 41% of those withdrawals.
That left the four platforms with a combined net outflow of $678 million, even as substantial amounts of Bitcoin circulated between their wallets.
Kraken also recorded significant outgoing transactions that day, including one involving approximately 4,028 BTC, illustrating the rapid movement of liquidity across exchanges during the downturn.
Bitcoin's supply squeeze faces a demand problem
The exchange movements have become particularly significant as Bitcoin struggles to recover from its recent decline below $60,000.
Although declining exchange reserves can reduce the amount of Bitcoin immediately available for sale, sustained buying demand remains essential to turning that scarcity into upward price pressure.
That demand has weakened considerably among US institutional investors.
According to Farside Investors, US spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded $1.7 billion in net withdrawals last week, extending a period of heavy redemptions that has stripped billions of dollars from the funds this month.
While Bitcoin subsequently recovered above $61,000 on Nov. 23, the ETF withdrawals have yet to show a corresponding recovery in institutional appetite.
The next test arrives Wednesday, when the US Bureau of Economic Analysis publishes October's personal consumption expenditures inflation report alongside its second estimate of third-quarter economic growth.
Both releases are scheduled for 8:30 a.m. ET and could influence expectations for the Federal Reserve's December interest rate decision.
Stronger inflation could push Treasury yields and the dollar higher, adding pressure to Bitcoin at a time when ETF investors are withdrawing capital.
That leaves Bitcoin's recovery dependent on two developments: exchange reserves continuing to decline across trading venues and fresh buying demand returning to absorb available supply.
If ETF withdrawals persist while Bitcoin continues circulating between exchanges, the apparent supply squeeze may offer little support against another wave of selling.

articles.title: GPT-6 Astra and Opus 5.5 expose a blind spot in AI oversight
articles.text:
Quick Take
- Leading AI models’ median placements fell between the 96th and 98th percentiles across 15 historical programming contests.
- Opus 5.5 rated GPT-6 Astra’s proposed tests about 0.2 points higher on average than METR’s human scorer did on a 0–1 scale.
- METR said a rating gap that large could change whether its rubric recommended investing more time in a proposed test.
In METR’s test of AI oversight, Opus 5.5 gave GPT-6 Astra’s proposed AI tests higher scores than the human evaluator did. METR said the gap could change whether its scoring rules recommended pursuing a test. In a separate exercise, leading AI agents placed ahead of most human entrants across 15 past programming contests.
Across Al Zimmermann’s programming contests, METR reported median placements from the 96th to the 98th percentile for Fable 5.1, Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra. About four people still beat the strongest models in the median contest.
The agents had 48 hours per contest on a 28-core machine. Each submission gave them a numerical score they could use to see whether their changes improved the result. Human contestants typically had about three calendar months, used their own hardware and could see the public standings. METR compared the agents’ scores with the original contest results.
Where AI oversight becomes a judgment call
In a separate exercise, METR asked agents to design tests that would help researchers assess what AI models could do. AI judges and a human scorer had access to project files, scores from trial runs and the agents’ case for why their tests were relevant and feasible. The human scorer assessed whether each proposed test was worth including in METR’s suite. METR said none of the designs was useful enough to include in its report.
The AI judges tended to agree more closely with the human scorer when a weaker model had designed the test. When the model that designed the test was as capable as the judge or stronger, the judges tended to rate the work more highly than the human did. Opus 5.5 agreed most closely with the human scorer, yet rated GPT-6 Astra’s proposals about 0.2 points higher on average on a scale from zero to one.
The comparison came from one exercise, and what counted as useful depended in part on METR’s research priorities. METR said models underused some resources in the judgment tests. It also reported strong model performance on some longer machine-learning tasks with automatic scoring. A separate AI peer review audit tested whether reviewers’ objections changed the findings by running code on the underlying data.
METR set score-and-time benchmarks for 34 of its 36 new tasks. It used direct human baselines for three and researcher estimates for the other 31.
METR said a gap that large could change whether the rubric recommended spending more time on a test.

articles.title: Bitcoin ETFs Shed $1.8b in Third-Largest Weekly Outflow
articles.text:
Bitcoin ETFs shed $1.8B in third-largest weekly outflow
Bitcoin ETF outflows reached $4.14 billion in November through Friday, nearing June’s $4.51 billion total.
US spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds (ETFs) recorded $1.79 billion in net outflows last week, their third-largest weekly total since the funds began trading in January 2024.
The record was $2.61 billion in the week ended Feb. 28, 2025, according to SoSoValue data. The week ended June 26 ranked second, with about $2 million more in net outflows than last week, based on the reported daily figures.
Investors withdrew a net $4.34 billion over four consecutive weeks, bringing year-to-date net outflows to roughly $3.8 billion.
BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT), the largest US spot Bitcoin ETF by assets, accounted for $1.37 billion, or about 76% of last week’s net outflows.
On Thursday, IBIT recorded $541.1 million in outflows, surpassing its previous daily high of $528.3 million on Jan. 30.
The fund broke that record again on Friday, with $544.7 million in net outflows, bringing the two-day total to $1.09 billion.
November net outflows across US spot Bitcoin ETFs reached $4.14 billion through Friday, about 8% below June’s record of $4.51 billion.
Bitcoin fell to just above $55,000 on Saturday, before recovering above $60,000 later that day.
Crypto trader Merlijn The Trader wrote on Sunday that Bitcoin (BTC) had fallen below the lowest band on the Rainbow Chart, a color-coded model that tracks Bitcoin’s long-term price trend.

articles.title: Strategy Buys $30M in Bitcoin, Moves $1B From USD Reserve to Cash Pot
articles.text:
In brief
- Strategy bought 457 BTC for $29.6 million last week, its fourth straight weekly purchase, lifting its holdings to 851,305 BTC, according to an SEC filing.
- Its board approved shifting $1 billion from the USD Reserve, which backs dividend and interest payments, to a cash account with broader uses.
- Strategy repurchased $211.8 million of STRC preferred stock and raised its buyback program for preferred shares from $3 billion to $4 billion.
Strategy bought 457 BTC for $29.6 million last week and moved $1 billion out of the reserve that backs its dividend payments into a general-purpose cash account, the company said on Monday.
The Bitcoin treasury firm paid an average of $64,898 per coin between November 16 and November 22, according to an SEC filing. Its fourth straight weekly purchase lifted its holdings to 851,305 BTC, acquired for a total of $64.23 billion at an average of about $75,446 per coin.
Strategy has acquired 457 $BTC and repurchased $212M of $STRC. We increased our Digital Credit Securities Repurchase Program by $1B and reallocated $1B from our USD Reserve to USD Cash. As of 11/22/26, we hold 851,305 BTC and $4.8B of USD Assets. $MSTR https://t.co/Wklom6dzrm
— Michael Saylor (@saylor) November 23, 2026
At the current Bitcoin price of about $61,233, per Decrypt data, those holdings are worth about $52.1 billion, roughly $12.1 billion less than Strategy paid. Bitcoin fell as low as $55,298 over the weekend, its lowest level since September 2024.
Executive chairman Michael Saylor tweeted that, as of November 22, Strategy held 851,305 BTC and $4.8 billion in U.S. dollar assets.
Reserve shift
Strategy's board authorized management to move up to $1 billion from its USD Reserve, which is meant to cover dividends on its preferred stock and interest on its debt, to its USD Cash account. Management can use that account for broader purposes, including buying Bitcoin, topping up the reserve and other capital management.
After the move, the USD Reserve stood at $3.73 billion and USD Cash at $1.09 billion. The reserve held $4.77 billion on November 8, according to an earlier filing. Strategy drew $17.6 million from it to pay preferred dividends last week.
Will Strategy hold over 1M BTC before 2027?
Bigger buyback program
Strategy repurchased 2,183,747 shares of STRC, its variable-rate preferred stock, for $211.8 million, down from $228 million the week before. It funded the Bitcoin purchase and $147 million of the buyback by selling 1,925,676 shares of MSTR stock for $176.7 million in net proceeds, and paid the remaining $64.8 million from USD Cash.
The board also raised the cap on its digital credit securities repurchase program, which covers its preferred stock, from $3 billion to $4 billion, leaving $1.12 billion available. Before the increase, about $120 million remained, after two weeks of STRC buybacks totaling about $440 million. Another $1 billion remains available to buy back MSTR stock.
The changes come a week before index provider MSCI removes MSTR from its MSCI USA Index after trading closes on November 30, which also takes it out of broader benchmarks such as the MSCI World index. Strategy has estimated that funds linked to MSCI indexes hold about 13 million of its shares.

articles.title: Strategy raises its buyback ceiling to $4 billion as MSTR shares sink 21%
articles.text:
Quick Take
- Strategy expanded its STRC buyback program for the third time to $4 billion after spending nearly $2.9 billion repurchasing preferred shares.
- MSTR shares have fallen 21% since July, while fresh stock issuance helped fund buybacks that reduced gross Bitcoin per diluted share by 0.37%.
- With STRC still below $100, Strategy must decide whether to deploy another $1 billion toward preferred-share support or Bitcoin accumulation.
Strategy raised its STRC buyback authorization for the third time on Monday, bringing the program to $4 billion as its common shares continued to struggle.
The Bitcoin treasury company had exhausted nearly $2.88 billion, or nearly 96% of its previous $3 billion authorization, after spending another $211.8 million repurchasing STRC during the week ended Nov. 22.
The latest expansion comes as Strategy's common shares have fallen 21.1% since it announced its first STRC repurchases on July 27. MSTR closed at $77.80 on Nov. 20, compared with $98.65 nearly four months earlier.
Strategy launched its initial $1 billion digital credit repurchase program in June, then increased it to $2 billion in September and $3 billion in October. Monday's announcement marks the third consecutive $1 billion expansion, bringing cumulative expansion to $4 billion.
The growing commitment has coincided with a shift in how Strategy deploys money raised from common shareholders.
According to its latest SEC filing, the company issued 1.93 million MSTR shares last week, raising $176.7 million.
Of those proceeds, $147 million (83.2%) funded STRC repurchases, while only $29.6 million (16.8%) went toward acquiring 457 Bitcoin.
Strategy contributed another $64.8 million from existing cash to complete the $211.8 million preferred-share repurchase.
Weekly repurchase spending in US dollars, reported amounts are rounded to $0.1M.
The spending has helped reduce its future dividend obligations but has not kept STRC consistently near its $100 stated amount. The security closed at $93.60 on Nov. 20, despite Strategy maintaining a 12% annual dividend rate to support its price.
Meanwhile, Strategy retains a separate $1 billion authorization to repurchase MSTR shares, which remained entirely unused last week.
Is Strategy's Bitcoin per share falling?
Bitcoin analyst Derin Olenik criticized the continued issuance of common shares to finance preferred-share repurchases, arguing the transactions weaken shareholders' underlying Bitcoin exposure.
Strategy's published figures support a decline in gross Bitcoin holdings per assumed diluted share during the latest reporting week.
Its outstanding Bitcoin balance increased from 850,849 BTC on Nov. 15 to 851,305 BTC on Nov. 22, while assumed diluted shares outstanding rose from approximately 457.24 million to 459.19 million.
Consequently, gross Bitcoin per share declined from approximately 186,082 satoshis to 185,392 satoshis, a reduction of about 690 satoshis (0.37%).
However, Strategy executive chairman Michael Saylor defended the transactions, arguing that Strategy's approach has consistently increased shareholders' net Bitcoin exposure despite the dilution.
He said:
“Our trades accreted Net BPS in each of the last 13 weeks. Cumulatively, we increased Net BPS by 584 sats/share and generated a Net BTC Gain of 2,505 BTC or $199M before preferred dividends, measured at a fixed $BTC price each week.”
Strategy-reported positive weekly contributions to net BTC per common share (in satoshis) before preferred dividends and holding BTC price fixed within each week. Values are transcribed from the supplied Strategy-branded Nov. 23 chart at one-decimal precision.
Saylor also reported that the latest week's transactions increased Net Bitcoin Per Share by six satoshis and improved Strategy's Net Reserve by $183 million.
The conflicting figures reflect competing assessments of Strategy's capital allocation. Gross Bitcoin per share measures its holdings against diluted shares, while Strategy's Net Bitcoin Per Share accounts for senior claims and dollar assets when calculating the Bitcoin exposure attributable to common shareholders.
Under Saylor's framework, retiring preferred securities can increase net exposure even when common-share issuance reduces gross Bitcoin holdings per share.
Olenik remained critical of the economics, questioning whether the increasingly complex transactions justify the continued dilution of common shareholders.
He also challenged the economics of STRC repurchases. His calculations put the security's average issuance price at $95.81 and its average repurchase price at $97.93, meaning Strategy has spent more buying back preferred shares than it originally received per share issued.
Average price estimated by dividing reported weekly spending, rounded to $0.1M, by shares repurchased. Per-share cents are approximate.
Strategy has defended repurchases below STRC's $100 stated amount because retiring the securities reduces future dividend obligations.
Saylor said Strategy has reduced outstanding credit by $2.9 billion in recent months, lowering annual dividend obligations by approximately $353 million.
The latest transactions alone retired 2.18 million STRC shares, eliminating approximately $26.2 million in annualized dividends at the current 12% rate.
Saylor shifts another $1 billion toward buybacks or Bitcoin
However, the company's latest decision suggests that reducing those obligations will remain a major capital priority.
Alongside the third buyback expansion, Strategy authorized transferring $1 billion from its dedicated USD Reserve into discretionary USD Cash, which management can use for further repurchases or Bitcoin purchases.
The change marks a departure from its original July policy, which explicitly prohibited using the USD Reserve to fund STRC repurchases.
Saylor said the reallocation was possible because the company's remaining reserve could cover its dividend and interest obligations for 3.4 years.
Following the adjustment, Strategy reported approximately $3.7 billion in dedicated reserves and over $1 billion in discretionary cash, leaving total dollar assets at roughly $4.8 billion.
Olenik interpreted the move as evidence that Strategy was preparing to rely more heavily on existing liquidity when issuing MSTR shares becomes less attractive.
That would let Strategy continue retiring preferred securities without relying entirely on new common-share issuance, although the company has not committed the reallocated cash to a specific purchase.
Strategy now has $1.1 billion in remaining preferred-share buyback authority, nearly matching its discretionary cash balance.
Its next capital-allocation decision will determine whether the expanded financial resources support further STRC repurchases or reverse the recent pattern of relatively modest Bitcoin purchases and continued MSTR dilution.

articles.title: Trump Again Urges Nvidia to Reinstate Jensen Huang
articles.text:
Trump renews call for Nvidia to rehire Jensen Huang as CEO
In a Truth Social post on Monday, Trump said rehiring Jensen Huang would benefit both Nvidia and the US.
US President Donald Trump has again urged Nvidia’s board to rehire co-founder Jensen Huang, days after the chipmaker said it did not intend to reinstate him.
“I hope the Board of Nvidia rehires Jensen Huang. It would be the best thing for the Company, and also, for the U.S.A.,” Trump wrote in a Monday post on Truth Social.
Trump had already called for Huang’s return on Friday, telling reporters after his trip to Asia that he wanted the former Nvidia chief to “make a big apology and go back.”
Trump’s remarks come after US Treasury Scott Bessent also seemingly softened his earlier calls for the company’s board to implement a “dramatic shake-up” of the company and to look outside for new leadership.
Asked Sunday if Trump’s recent support for Huang contradicted his own call, Bessent declined to say whether Huang should return.
“I think we have to see where the buck stops,” he said, referring to any potential non-compliance with US export controls.
Polymarket shows traders have placed a 37% chance that Huang will rejoin Nvidia by Dec. 31, 2027.
Related: Nvidia shares fall 4% as board reportedly rules out Huang return

articles.title: Czech Authorities Charge 15 Over $12M Unlicensed Crypto Casino
articles.text:
In brief
- Czech customs and police have charged 15 people over BETFIN, an unlicensed online casino built on Polygon, and estimate the group's unlawful gains at $12 million.
- Twenty people were detained in October raids involving nearly 300 officers and Europol staff. Three alleged organizers are in custody and face up to 13.5 years.
- Investigators said the casino was centrally controlled despite its decentralized branding, used bots to inflate player numbers and issued billions of tokens.
Czech customs officers and police have charged 15 people over BETFIN, a crypto casino that investigators say operated without a gambling license while presenting itself as a decentralized project, authorities said on Thursday.
The group's unlawful gains so far total about 267 million koruna ($12.1 million), according to a joint statement from the Czech customs service and the National Centre Against Organised Crime (NCOZ). Officers detained 20 people and searched more than 40 homes and other premises in October, in an operation involving nearly 300 customs officers and police, as well as Europol staff.
Three alleged organizers are being held in custody. Those charged are accused of participating in an organized criminal group and operating gambling without a license, and the main organizers face up to 13.5 years in prison if convicted. Authorities seized assets worth about 100 million koruna ($4.5 million), including property, vehicles, jewelry, cash and crypto.
The agencies described it as the first Czech case in which suspected illegal gambling centered on a decentralized online casino using blockchain infrastructure, smart contracts and its own token.
When will Polymarket's POLY TGE?
How BETFIN worked
BETFIN presented itself as a decentralized casino with its own token traded on decentralized exchanges. Investigators hired a specialist firm to examine its smart contracts on the Polygon network, and analyzed more than 2.3 million bets placed by about 28,500 players. The project was promoted on social media, Telegram and Discord, as well as in online videos and at conferences.
Users could join in two ways, Michal Šimůnek, director of the customs service's search and supervision section, told a press conference near Prague on Thursday, according to the Czech News Agency (ČTK). They could buy tokens to play casino games such as roulette, or buy them as investors and become co-owners of the casino. Despite its decentralized branding, the group ran a centrally controlled system, he said.
A large share of player accounts were created by automated programs to inflate activity, Šimůnek said. "This created the casino's supposed profit, which was then redistributed to investors," he said, in comments translated from Czech.
Developers issued billions of tokens and steered investors to buy them off-exchange, which let the group raise money without moving the token's market price, Šimůnek added. Customs officers also found that the declared value of all tokens in circulation, more than 45 billion koruna ($2 billion), far exceeded the roughly 11 million koruna ($500,000) of liquidity on exchanges.
Czech news site Seznam Zprávy reported the raids in October, saying those detained included YouTubers who had promoted BETFIN, and that the project's token had already fallen close to zero in 2025.
The token, BET, has fallen further since. It traded at about $0.000001 on Monday, more than 99.9% below its all-time high of $0.002906, and hit a new all-time low within the past week, according to CoinGecko data. Its 24-hour trading volume was about $1,100, with both CoinGecko and CoinMarketCap putting its total supply at around 777.8 billion tokens.
NCOZ deputy director Petr Danko said using blockchain technology is not illegal, but using it outside the law is. The Czech state is the injured party, he said, because the group was required to obtain authorization to run gambling. Whether investors suffered losses will depend on the ongoing investigation, he added.
The High Prosecutor's Office in Olomouc is overseeing the case. Criminal proceedings are continuing, and authorities said they could not share further details.

articles.title: Bill Ackman Warns Continued Fed Rate Hikes Risk Recession
articles.text:
Billionaire Bill Ackman warns Fed will make a rate ‘mistake’ in December
Markets and economists widely expect the US Federal Reserve to raise interest rates by 25 basis points in its December meeting.
Billionaire investor Bill Ackman warned Sunday that the Federal Reserve risks pushing the US and the world into recession if it keeps raising interest rates to try to bring inflation back to 2%, arguing that financial conditions have already tightened “massively.”
In an X post, the hedge fund manager argued that the required investment in global military spending, tariffs, and massive investment in AI infrastructure and energy means that 3% inflation should be a more realistic target for the Fed.
“The Fed will put the US and world in recession if it continues to raise rates in a failed attempt to drive inflation to 2%,” he said.
Ackman’s comments came a day after US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent cited hawkish remarks from Fed officials as one factor behind last week’s stock market sell-off.
“Many people believe that they may be making a policy mistake if they overtighten,” Bessent told CBS on Sunday.
The warning comes as Federal Reserve officials remain divided on rate hikes.
In October, the Federal Reserve held its benchmark rate at 3.75% to 4% in a 10–2 vote in October, with both dissenters favoring a quarter-point hike.
One of the dissenters was Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook, who on Friday argued that financial conditions were still too accommodative to bring inflation back to 2%.
She said it was estimated that inflation reached 3.8% in October and warned that delaying rate increases could force the central bank to raise rates more sharply later.
“In a different environment, the Committee could afford to be patient, but I continue to believe that in this economic climate we do not have that luxury,” she said.
The next decision is due Dec. 9, with CME FedWatch putting the odds of a December quarter-point hike at about 91.2% at the time of writing.
Related: Fed officials saw October rate hold as a ‘close call,’ minutes show

articles.title: Solana Meme Coin for Fiona the Hippo Raises $100K for Cincinnati Zoo Charity
articles.text:
In brief
- Fiona, the Cincinnati Zoo's famous pygmy hippo, died on November 19 after swallowing a visitor's hat that was accidentally launched into her enclosure.
- A Pump.fun meme coin made in her honor hit a $3.52 million market cap and has donated more than $103,000 to the Zoological Society of Cincinnati.
- The token has since dropped 52%, and traders are betting it can follow Moo Deng's meme coin success of 2024.
Fiona the Hippo, a fan-favorite pygmy hippo at the Cincinnati Zoo, died last week after swallowing a hat that accidentally ended up in her enclosure. Crypto bros have created a meme coin in her honor—raising $100,000 for charity in the process.
The tragic death came after a visitor tossed their knitted hat in the air, which then got caught by a ceiling fan and flung it through a small window into Fiona's habitat. The pygmy hippo lost her appetite as the hat got stuck in her small intestine, and veterinary staff tried their best to help Fiona pass the hat naturally—as surgery was deemed too risky. Unfortunately, Fiona died on Thursday, November 19, at nine years old.
As is often the case, crypto bros rushed to create a Solana meme coin that surged to a $3.52 million market capitalization the day after Fiona's death. It has since dropped more than 50% to $1.5 million, per DEX Screener.
Fiona the hippo has died after she ate a visitor's hat that fell into her enclosure at the Cincinnati Zoo. pic.twitter.com/YHbjoEEDhb
— Pop Base (@PopBase) November 19, 2026
The Pump.fun-created token is donating 100% of the generated creator rewards to the Zoological Society of Cincinnati, the non-profit that runs the zoo and its scientific programs. So far, according to Donate.gg, $103,600 has been donated.
But, of course, profits are at the forefront of crypto traders' minds. One of the top traders turned a $1,637 investment into $43,800 in a matter of days, according to DEX Screener.
"I feel like animals are often treated more like attractions for people than living beings. Their safety and lives should come first, not just entertaining visitors," pseudonymous trader Athena Alpha told Decrypt. "This isn’t even the first time something like this has happened."
Will HYPE flip SOL in 2026?
The most famous example happened in the same zoo. Endangered gorilla Harambe was fatally shot at the Cincinnati Zoo a decade ago, after a young boy fell into his habitat. This sparked global outrage, as the gorilla was killed through no fault of his own. In turn, Harambe became one of the most viral memes of the 2010s.
"I think stricter action needs to be taken against both visitors and zoo officials to make sure things like this don’t happen again," the trader said. "Honestly, I feel like a big part of the problem is the lack of accountability and consequences. Unless people are held responsible, nothing is really going to change."
Gone too soon. Way too soon.
The Cincinnati Zoo needs to ensure something like this can never happen again. https://t.co/vWeb8ekyVw pic.twitter.com/hqt35SOcP6
— Nati Sports (@Nati_Sports) November 19, 2026
This story has hit particularly hard, as Fiona was a beloved animal whose premature birth in 2017 drew attention. At birth, zoo keepers had to care for her because she was too small for her mother to look after. Fortunately, she survived this tough start to life and went on to become one of the zoo's most famous animals.
People's love for Fiona may have been boosted by the rise of Moo Deng, a cute pygmy hippo who went mega viral in 2024. As with Fiona, crypto traders made an unofficial meme coin for Moo Deng, but this one went much higher—peaking at a $610 million market cap.
Naturally, traders have made the comparison between the two pygmy hippos, with some suggesting that the Moo Deng meme coin's success should mean similar gains for the Fiona token.
With Fiona's meme coin sitting at a $1.5 million market cap, that thesis has yet to be proven.
"If Fiona goes to $1 billion, her legacy will live forever all around the world," one trader tweeted. "Do it for Fiona!"

articles.title: Monad faces $190 million insider token unlock larger than its market cap as MON hits record low
articles.text:
Quick Take
- Monad is set to unlock 16.61 billion MON worth approximately $190 million on Nov. 24, exceeding its market cap as the token hits an all-time low.
- The release equals 140.5% of circulating supply, with team members and investors receiving 94% of the newly unlocked tokens.
- The unlock could intensify selling pressure and reshape validator voting power as insiders decide whether to sell, hold or stake their allocations.
Monad is preparing to unlock 16.61 billion MON tokens on Nov. 24, exceeding its circulating supply as the cryptocurrency hits record lows.
The release represents 140.5% of the 11.83 billion MON currently circulating and marks the first major insider distribution since the blockchain launched in November 2025.
According to DefiLlama, approximately 10.7 billion MON will go to team members, 4.925 billion to investors, and 987.5 million to the Category Labs treasury. This means its team and investor allocations account for 94% of the release.
The unlock was valued at approximately $226 million in Tokenomist's earlier estimate, but MON's decline has reduced its value to roughly $190 million, still exceeding the token's $137 million market capitalization.
CryptoSlate's data shows MON plunged around 11% over the past 24 hours, touching an all-time low of $0.01152 ahead of the release. It is trading at $0.012 as of press time.
The incoming supply adds to existing market pressure, with further insider distributions scheduled through 2029.
Historical data from Alea Research shows that 16 comparable token unlocks recorded median declines of 25.2% in the preceding month and 6.9% in the following month.
Category Labs has authorized up to $80 million in MON repurchases through Dec. 31, although Alea found no disclosed purchases under the program.
Insider staking could shift validator power
Beyond potential selling, the release could alter how Monad distributes voting power and staking rewards.
The network had 20.73 billion MON backing validator votes across 197 operators on Nov. 22, according to Valopers.
If insiders stake just 2.3 billion MON, approximately 14% of their newly available allocation, those tokens would account for 10% of the resulting voting power, assuming existing stake remains unchanged.
At 25% participation, approximately 4.15 billion MON would enter active staking, representing 16.7% of the expanded total.
That scenario would also reduce gross inflationary rewards per staked MON by 16.7%, assuming issuance and validator commissions remain constant.
The potential redistribution comes amid substantial concentration of Foundation-linked staking allocations.
Alea estimated that Foundation-linked wallets accounted for 78% of active stake on Nov. 1, while Backpack controlled 10.82% of validator voting weight on Nov. 22.
Monad initially prohibited staking locked insider tokens to direct more early rewards toward public holders. The restriction expires with the unlock, allowing newly eligible tokens to compete for staking rewards and validator influence.
The first post-unlock delegations will show whether insiders reinforce the largest validators or spread voting power across smaller operators, while trading activity will reveal how much of the new supply reaches exchanges.

articles.title: Trump Dinner Wallets Linked to Non-US Crypto Exchanges
articles.text:
Half of wallets on Trump’s dinner list got tokens from non-US exchanges
Public Citizen traced 66 of 130 qualifying wallets to exchanges that restrict US users, raising questions over who is attending Trump’s memecoin dinner on Sunday.
More than half the wallets that qualified for Donald Trump’s memecoin dinner on Sunday received TRUMP tokens from crypto exchanges that bar US users, according to analysis from consumer advocacy group Public Citizen.
Trump is hosting his second dinner for his top memecoin holders at Trump National Golf Club in Sterling, Virginia, more than a year after an inaugural dinner in May 2025. The dinner offers up to 185 seats based on time-weighted TRUMP holdings.
Public Citizen said it traced 66 of the 130 wallets on the public leaderboard to exchanges including Binance (the global exchange), Bybit and BloFin — which are not permitted to serve US citizens. The list also included 15 of the 29 wallets that qualified for a VIP reception with the president.
“If those bans are enforced, many of the people vying for a seat at the president’s table don’t live in the United States,” said Public Citizen research director Zach Everson.
Trump’s memecoin events have drawn scrutiny over whether foreign buyers can essentially buy access to the president. Democratic lawmakers called on the White House to release the guest list for the first dinner in May 2025, while some joined a protest outside the golf club. They renewed the request again in October.
Who qualified for Trump’s memecoin dinner?
FastX, a Singapore-linked crypto trading platform, was the top-ranked wallet, holding $1.65 million in TRUMP at the time of the snapshot on Nov. 16.
The third highest ranked wallet has been linked to Unitas, a stablecoin issuer run by a British Virgin Islands company, according to Public Citizen.
Morten Christensen, a crypto entrepreneur from the Netherlands and founder and CEO of AirdropAlert, shared a picture from the Trump gala dinner on X. He came 26th with $45,351 in time-weighted TRUMP holdings.
Public Citizen also identified 14 wallets it suspects were controlled by the same person or group. Each received approximately 3,700 TRUMP tokens from Binance in October before being emptied weeks ahead of the cutoff.
Related: ‘Lawyer up’: Democrats target Trump, Big Tech after midterm sweep
Tron founder Justin Sun, the top-ranked holder at the May 2025 dinner, was expected to skip the event, according to The Wall Street Journal.

Trump token down 99% from peak
